comments.author: @elenabogarin
comments.text:
I can agree that some Airbnb rules are ridiculous. But when people say, “I’d rather stay at a hotel because I don’t have to clean,” there’s a bigger picture being missed.

Most of the rules hosts have today exist because hosts have already been burned. These are people’s homes and investments not hotel rooms owned by huge corporations. We still have mortgages, electricity, water, maintenance, supplies, cleaners, and rising costs.

Guests have thrown parties, left vomit EVERYWHERE, left 10+ bags of trash, damaged things, ruined linens, and created hours of extra work. Some Airbnb cleaners charge $300–$500 for a normal turnover, and excessive mess can mean another cleaning charge on top of that.

I’ve absorbed those costs myself plenty of times, but eventually you can’t keep eating hundreds of dollars because a guest decided to leave the house trashed.

And yes, hotel housekeeping cleans up after you. But hotel housekeepers are employees. Many Airbnb cleaners are independent businesses that set their own rates and are not going to work for $100 to clean up someone’s disaster.

Not every guest is bad I’ve had amazing guests. But if you want to stay in someone’s home, basic respect for the home and the person cleaning it shouldn’t be controversial.

You don’t have to clean an Airbnb. But you also shouldn’t trash it because someone else is getting paid to clean.

I didn’t sleep the rest of the time I was there because I was terrified he would let himself in while I was sleeping.. 

I reported all of this to Airbnb and notified the police after I left just to let them know this was something of concern.. Airbnb never responded, and the police said, “ok, we will log this with the address incase something happens in the future.” I hope nothing happened..
